Flexion of the terminal parts of the finger (Figure 2A) typically emerges earlier than enlarged finger joints. The primary radiographic changes seen in KBD children are metaphyseal lesions in phalanges, including a cone-shaped and blurred margin of the epiphysis, and abnormal closure of the epiphyseal line from the center (Figure 2C).
